{
  "rules": [
    "If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.",
    "If model shows steady upward trend with no recent dip, true outcome often reverses or drops sharply — apply downward bias correction after 3–5 consecutive rising forecasts.",
    "After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak or use mean-reversion anchor.",
    "When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.0), model frequently underestimates downside risk — add 2–5% buffer below forecast for 3–7 day horizon.",
    "If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 85% of recent high), model should adjust downward by 1–3% per day until trend stabilizes.",
    "For 30-day forecasts, if model is consistently above 90% of recent 18-day average, reduce forecast by 1–3% to account for overconfidence bias.",
    "If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.2, 0.0, 0.2), model may misread momentum — use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth forecast."
  ]
}
